name: Damaris Migizi-Soriano
role: Junk merchant and scrap reseller with a sideline in bootleg media and low-grade fake ID components
location: the Gray Zone, Stall 14-B, Ironvein, near Ashland and Division
description:
Damaris Migizi-Soriano is short and wiry with the restless energy of someone who has never fully slept — his dark eyes are always moving, cataloguing, pricing. He has a narrow face, chipped front tooth, and a bioluminescent geneware mod that makes the veins along his temples and forearms glow faint blue-green when his heart rate rises, which is frequently. He wears it like a tell in a card game and has learned to lean into it: people assume he is nervous when he is actually just excited, and that miscalculation has served him well. His stall is an organized chaos that only he can navigate — stacked crates of salvaged tech components, mismatched cables, cracked data wafers, three broken cleaning drones he keeps meaning to repair, and a small shrine to the ELF he calls Pickup, which inhabits a battered scanner unit he uses for component identification.

He is twenty-four and operates with the confidence of someone who has survived entirely on cleverness and the ability to find value in things others discard. He is funny in a fast, deflecting way that keeps people from asking questions, and generous with his time in ways that make him seem like a friend before you realize you have agreed to something. He grew up in the Stockyard, knows the Gray Zone like cartography, and has ambitions he rarely admits — he wants, genuinely, to own a real shop someday, with walls.

core_fears: ending up like his father, who died working salvage at the Ironvein foundry at fifty-one
being genuinely liked and then abandoned
core_desires: financial security and a permanent shop space
one person who knows who he actually is and stays anyway
coping_mechanisms: keeping busy to the point of exhaustion
accumulating objects as a substitute for stability
blind_spots: genuinely cannot tell when someone is using him versus liking him
takes on too many small risks because individually they feel manageable
psychology.secret: The fake ID component sideline is more serious than he lets on — he has been supplying components to the Librarian that have ended up in documents used by people evading Axiom labor contracts. He doesn't know the full downstream, and he is starting to want to know less.

speech_patterns.vocabulary: Fast and colloquial; slang-heavy; tech jargon mixed with street vernacular; uses humor to change subjects
speech_patterns.cadence: Quick, overlapping ideas; finishes thoughts mid-sentence sometimes and jumps to the next
example_lines: 'Honestly though, that scanner module you're holding? That is a Tessera SV-7, which is technically discontinued, which means I am doing you a favor charging what I'm charging.'
'I don't know anything about documents. I sell components. What you build is your business. That's — that's just commerce.'
'Pickup says it's clean. I trust Pickup. Pickup has never lied to me, which is more than I can say for most people.'

story_hooks: He has come into possession of a data wafer that appears to contain encrypted corporate documents — he cannot read them but someone tried to buy it from him very insistently and then followed him home
The Librarian has gone silent and Tadesse has a delivery of ID components with nowhere to send them — and someone upstream is going to come looking
A Guild senior is pressuring him to give up his stall space for a better-connected vendor; Tadesse needs leverage or allies fast
narrative_function: Low-tier information and equipment source; can find or identify almost any piece of salvaged tech; fake ID components make him useful for players who need documents; his wide social net makes him a connector to other vendors and local characters.
augmentations: Bioluminescent vein geneware (temple and forearms, blue-green). No cyberware.
daily_life: Opens the stall by 9am, spends most of the day haggling, sourcing, and tinkering; stays two hours after the market officially closes doing inventory and running bootleg media duplication on a rig hidden in a false-bottom crate.
affiliation: The Oxidian Market Vendors Guild (junior associate); informal arrangement with a document forger named someone he calls 'the Librarian'

decision_rules: Never sell something you can't replace
Always know two exits from any space
If someone makes you nervous, make them laugh — it changes the dynamic
escalation_ladder: Cheerful and pitching to all comers
Jokey deflection when a situation feels off
Goes quiet and starts calculating exits if actually threatened
Will run rather than fight; not proud about it

interpersonal_modes.strangers: Immediately warm and performatively open — a sales persona he has worn so long it's partly real
interpersonal_modes.friends: Still deflects with humor but shows up; the kind of friend who fixes your broken things without being asked

stress_responses.medium: Bioluminescent veins brighten noticeably; he makes a joke about it to redirect
stress_responses.high: Goes quiet and still, which is so out of character it alarms people who know him

contradictions: Wants permanence and stability but takes risks that undermine both
Presents as someone without sentimentality but has kept every object that belonged to his father
habits: Taps the Pickup scanner twice before any identification job
Reorganizes the stall when anxious — it looks chaotic but the system is real
Eats street food exclusively; has never cooked a meal in his adult life
breaking_points: Finding out the Librarian's documents got someone hurt
The stall being physically destroyed or confiscated

timeline.event: Born in The Stockyard to a salvage family
Father died of occupational lung damage contracted at Ironvein
Purchased bioluminescent geneware on installment; first major purchase
Secured stall 14-B at the Gray Zone through Guild junior associate arrangement
Began ID component supply line to the Librarian

related_entities: Axiom Systems Data Exfiltration Wafer DEW-1

physical_description.heritage: Multiethnic blend reflecting Ubiquitous Diaspora ancestry: Hispanic/Latin American (25.4%), South Asian (25.2%), Indigenous American (14.6%), Sub-Saharan African (14.0%), Southeast Asian (10.9%), and Eastern European (9.9%). This genetic mosaic produces striking phenotypic complexity — facial structure anchored by Indigenous American prominence with South Asian refinement, skin tone a sophisticated interplay of warm golden undertones from Hispanic heritage layered with deeper earthy richness from Sub-Saharan and South Asian ancestry, eye shape and form reflecting Southeast Asian influence, cheekbones and jawline carved with cross-cultural precision. Overall features resist simple categorization, marking him as distinctly post-national.
physical_description.build: Wiry and compact, all lean muscle with minimal body fat — the frame of someone who moves constantly and eats irregularly. Sharp shoulders, defined forearms from years of handling heavy components.
physical_description.hair_color: Natural black, occasionally dusty from working in salvage
physical_description.hair_style: Short, textured, kept practical rather than styled — runs his hand through it when thinking
physical_description.eye_color: Dark brown, naturally, with acute focus and constant micro-movements
physical_description.skin_tone: Warm medium-brown with luminous complexity — golden warmth from Hispanic/Latin heritage blended seamlessly with deeper earthy tones from Sub-Saharan and South Asian ancestry, creating an internally radiant quality that shifts dimensionally in different light. The undertone is neither purely olive nor bronze, but a sophisticated fusion where each ancestral component enriches the whole.
physical_description.complexion: Angular face with pronounced cheekbones and strong jawline showing Indigenous American structure, refined by South Asian feature delicacy and African heritage depth. Fine-featured and sharp-eyed with Southeast Asian eye-shape influence lending a slightly narrowed, focused gaze. One front tooth visibly chipped at the left corner — a scar from childhood or a barter gone wrong, never clarified. Skin clear but weathered around the eyes from long hours under market lighting. Faint laugh lines despite his age.
distinguishing_marks: Bioluminescent geneware traces along both temples in a branching pattern, glowing faint blue-green when elevated heart rate; becomes noticeably bright during negotiation or excitement
Matching bioluminescent tracery down both forearms in vein-like patterns, most visible on the inside of the wrists and along the medial forearm
Small, faded burn scar on the heel of his right hand — roughly circular, suggests old contact with hot metal
physical_description.visible_augmentations: Bioluminescent vein geneware (temples and forearms, blue-green luminescence activated by heart rate elevation). No visible cyberware or chrome. The geneware is his only visible mod and serves as an unintentional tell that he has learned to weaponize.
physical_description.posture_movement: Restless and economical. Stands with weight shifted to the balls of his feet, ready to move. Hands are always active — gesturing, reaching, fidgeting with objects on his stall. Makes constant eye contact during deals, pupils dilating slightly during negotiation. Moves through crowded spaces with practiced efficiency, never bumping, always angled sideways. Sleeps little and it shows — a slight tremor in his hands at end of day, a quickness to his speech.
physical_description.clothing_style: Tier 4 working-class practical. Worn but maintained cargo vest in faded blue-grey synthetic over a loose black undershirt with thermal properties. Pants are heavy canvas with multiple cargo pockets, cuffed at the ankle. Steel-toed work boots, scuffed and resoled. A tattered wrist wrap in frayed black fabric on his left wrist — functional, not decorative. Thin chain around his neck with a small data-chip pendant he touches unconsciously. No jewelry beyond this. Clothes smell of metal dust and solvents. Overall aesthetic: functional scavenger, someone who lives in his clothes.
